We have a big first aid kit but recently I've been getting into treating more trauma. Was curious what you guys managed to squirrel away?
What level of medical prep do you have?

I have:

2 duplicate basic first aid kits for around-the-house booboos... (hate that word but it suits it best)

2 duplicate comprehensive first aid kits in MOLLE bag for the car and getting home in an incident. Nothing for true trauma but it will stop you from bleeding out, hold minor to moderate cuts, tiny flashlight, etc. Also has basic first aid kit attached to it. The bag is MOLLE to allow me easy transfer from stand-alone/get home to a bug out bag.

2 duplicate comprehensive trauma kits. These are the supplies that are "omg, if I don't use this, someone will die." Things for gunshot wounds, tourniquets, Israeli bandage, covering chest wounds (and ventilation), blood clotting agents, scalpels, etc. Again, MOLLE bags for attachment and transfer, if needed.

Everything in all kits are vacuum sealed using a food saver to prevent drying out, water damage, contamination, etc. Vacuum sealing also makes nearly everything take up far less room than it would otherwise.. All kits include either a knife or x-acto blade to open the seals (or for unforeseens).

Kits are duplicated and identical because I have a teen living with me and if he's still around when shit goes down, he has a kit as well. If he's not, then I have an emergency back-up medical setup.
